bottom_line: The Fed (the people who set interest rates) is getting ready to raise rates again because prices are still rising too fast. That would make loans and credit cards cost more, and it's a big reason stocks fell hard today, even on the day of a record AI IPO.

stories.title: The Fed wants higher rates
stories.real: Several Fed officials say they want more rate hikes. They disagree only on how fast. Fed member Goolsbee says inflation (prices going up) is 'way higher' than the Fed's 2% target, and J.P. Morgan expects hikes at the next three meetings.
stories.you: Borrowing for a car, a house or on a credit card could get more expensive, and traders are betting rates stay high for years.

stories.title: Anthropic's IPO didn't lift tech
stories.real: Anthropic, the company that makes the Claude AI chatbot, started trading on the Nasdaq. Its shares jumped 27% and it was valued at $1.8 trillion. Other tech stocks still fell, and SoftBank in Japan plunged over 16%.
stories.you: A big, splashy debut for one company didn't end investors' worries about AI stocks, and those stocks make up a large part of many retirement funds.

stories.title: Chip companies in trouble over China
stories.real: Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang resigned, and California's attorney general has now subpoenaed Nvidia (legally ordered it to hand over information) about AI chips ending up in China. Separately, AMD fell over 7% after a short seller (an investor who makes money when a stock falls) claimed its technology turned up at a blacklisted Chinese company. AMD says it follows U.S. law.
stories.you: Nvidia is tied to a lot of other companies, so its legal trouble can drag down a large part of the stock market.

stories.you: Most jobs look safe for now, but everyday costs like fuel are still putting pressure on household budgets.
